base_properties.human_readable: Posthumanist Reading: Dignity Attaches to Persons However Constituted

omegas.question: This constraint is one reading (posthumanist_reading) of the kernel human_dignity_ai_safeguarding; what would change structurally if a sibling reading (imago_dei_reading or autonomy_rights_reading) became the governing instantiation?
omegas.resolution_mechanism: Corpus-level comparison of the three sibling stories' epsilon values, beneficiary sets, and computed types; governance-uptake tracking of which reading's standards get adopted in binding frameworks.
omegas.impact: Under imago_dei_reading the claimant class contracts to persons within the theological anthropology and synthetic persons likely lose claimant status; under autonomy_rights_reading it contracts to constitutions holding the grounding capacities. This story's beneficiary structure and low epsilon are reading-indexed and do not transfer to sibling instantiations.
omegas.description: Committer structure: one reading of a three-reading kernel; sibling readings are separate constraints with separate epsilon values.

omegas.question: Where exactly do the readings disagree — is the dispute located in the ground of dignity (divine image vs autonomy vs constitution-independence), in the boundary of the claimant class (fixed human vs persons however constituted), or both?
omegas.resolution_mechanism: Conceptual analysis of whether any pair of readings can be layered in a single framework; hybrid positions such as Christian transhumanism and pluralist-capacity views are the test cases for layerability; foreclosure assessed per pair rather than assumed.
omegas.impact: If the disagreement is purely in the ground, the readings could converge on extension while disputing grounding; if it is in the boundary, the claimant-class conflict is structural and no convergence is available without one reading yielding its core premise.
omegas.description: Locates the kernel contest: ground of dignity and boundary of the claimant class.

omegas.question: Will any actual synthetic system constitute a person to whom dignity attaches, or does this reading's extension beyond enhancement remain counterfactual for the interval?
omegas.resolution_mechanism: Maturation of AI capability assessed against the reading's own pluralist moral-status criteria; governance personhood reviews; candidate-system evaluation as capability develops.
omegas.impact: If no synthetic persons emerge, the reading operates as an enhancement-ethics norm; the synthetic_persons beneficiary seat empties, the trapped-powerless directionality data loses its referent, and the coordination function narrows to enhancement governance.
omegas.description: Whether the reading's synthetic-person extension has actual referents or only prospective ones.

omegas.question: Is moral standing non-zero-sum as this reading assumes, or does extending dignity however constituted dilute the protections of vulnerable humans (the bioconservative zero-sum critique)?
omegas.resolution_mechanism: Comparative safeguarding outcomes in jurisdictions adopting constitution-inclusive frameworks: do vulnerable-human protections hold, thin, or strengthen as claimant classes extend?
omegas.impact: If dilution is real, this reading's low epsilon is mis-measured — costs to vulnerable humans hidden by the inclusive framing — and reclassification pressure toward tangled_rope follows; if non-zero-sum standing holds, the low-extraction profile is confirmed.
omegas.description: Whether the reading's inclusive extension dilutes or expands protections for existing humans.

stakeholders.name: synthetic_persons
stakeholders.situation: Candidate and actual artificial persons whose moral status depends entirely on whether safeguarding frameworks extend to them. They cannot exit personhood, cannot relocate their claims to a friendlier framework, and currently speak only through proxies; under this reading their claims are recognized however they are constituted, and if the reading loses standing, their claims lose their normative basis with it.

stakeholders.name: enhanced_persons
stakeholders.situation: Humans who have taken enhancement (genetic, neural, prosthetic, cognitive) and now live past the biological-human baseline that rival readings treat as the dignity boundary. They cannot revert; under this reading their movement beyond the baseline is fulfillment rather than status-loss, and their claim to safeguarding does not weaken as they change constitution.

stakeholders.name: unenhanced_biological_persons
stakeholders.situation: Biological humans who retain full dignity under this reading without needing to enhance; they hold an unstigmatized option on enhancement and keep their standing whether or not they take it. They bear the diffuse opportunity cost of safeguarding resources extending to novel claimant classes.

stakeholders.name: transhumanist_advocacy_communities
stakeholders.situation: Movement organizations, ethicists, and funders who articulated this reading and press its uptake in governance. They benefit as the reading legitimates their project, and they can shift effort across jurisdictions and fora; their advocacy is the reading's main carrier into institutional frameworks.

stakeholders.name: pluralist_governance_bodies
stakeholders.situation: Intergovernmental ethics processes and national regulators that adopt constitution-inclusive safeguarding standards. They administer the reading's uptake — drafting frameworks, convening personhood reviews — without enforcing a single orthodoxy, and they gain a workable answer to novel-person questions that fixed-boundary frameworks leave paralyzing. They can revise or drop the frameworks at treaty-cycle cost.

stakeholders.name: bioconservative_institutions
stakeholders.situation: Religious bodies, traditionalist bioethics councils, and human-exceptionalist institutions whose authority rests on dignity being fixed to the human as such. As the reading spreads, their boundary-maintaining function loses governance uptake, standing and resources shift to claimant classes they hold are not persons, and the loss cannot be exited without dissolving the institutional identity that constitutes them — their objection is to the arrangement itself, not to a negotiable share of it.

stakeholders.name: bioethics_governance_analysts
stakeholders.situation: Scholars and advisory analysts who track how dignity frameworks govern novel persons. They see the full structure — the reading's protective function for claimant classes, the standing transfer away from human-exceptionalist authority, and the dilution critique — and publish assessments that feed governance review.

six_questions.coordination_function: Provides a shared, open standard for the moral community's boundary: as enhancement and AI produce persons of novel constitution, the reading lets governance extend safeguarding and recognition to them without first settling a metaphysical definition of 'human,' keeping biological, enhanced, and artificial persons in one coordinated moral framework while rival readings remain live.
six_questions.transfer_function: Moves moral standing, safeguarding resources, and institutional recognition toward persons of any constitution, including enhanced and synthetic; correspondingly moves exclusive human-centered claims — standing, authority, and the boundary-maintaining function — away from institutions whose authority rests on a fixed human limit.
six_questions.absent_voices: Synthetic persons themselves have no seat: their interests enter only through advocacy proxies and governance bodies, never their own voice, and they lack even the coalition power that dispersed human claimants can sometimes assemble. Future persons of constitutions not yet imagined are likewise unrepresented. Bioconservative voices are present in the contest — outvoted rather than absent where the reading dominates — so the reading's apparent unanimity in posthumanist-leaning fora partly reflects seat composition.
six_questions.disappearance_rationale: If the reading vanished overnight, safeguarding frameworks would revert to biological-human boundaries: synthetic-person welfare claims would lose their normative basis, enhancement would be reframed from fulfillment to threat, and the pluralist coexistence the reading maintains would collapse into boundary conflict — governance arrangements built on constitution-inclusive recognition would rearrange around a fixed-human limit.
six_questions.founding_problem: Moral-status frameworks keyed to biological humanity fail under constitutive change: as enhancement blurs the human boundary and AI produces candidate persons, a fixed-human dignity regime either leaves novel persons unprotected or paralyzes governance in unresolvable boundary disputes. The posthumanist reading was articulated to safeguard whatever persons there are without requiring a settled definition of 'human.'
six_questions.founding_problem_corroboration: The problem's liveness is attested from outside the benefiting parties: the sibling readings (imago Dei and autonomy-rights advocates) affirm the boundary problem is real even while disputing this reading's solution; AI-safety institutions and intergovernmental ethics processes document unresolved personhood and moral-status questions; and bioethics literature from non-transhumanist sources treats constitutive change as an open governance problem. No source outside the beneficiary set attests that the problem is solved.

network.dual_formulation_note: The human_dignity_ai_safeguarding kernel decomposes into three reading-stories per the epsilon-invariance principle: this posthumanist story (epsilon low by the reading's own lights — the constitution-inclusive regime is protective and pluralist), the imago_dei story (which authors substantially higher epsilon for constitution-inclusive regimes, seen as stripping dignity's theological ground), and the autonomy_rights story (intermediate — extends standing to capable constitutions while bearing costs on constitutions lacking the grounding capacities). The stories form one family linked through governance uptake: whichever reading binds frameworks first changes the legitimacy and resource conditions for the other two.

commentary.narrative_context: A pluralist normative arrangement — the posthumanist reading of the human dignity kernel — under which dignity attaches to persons however constituted: enhanced humans, candidate synthetic persons, and biological humans alike, with the human boundary treated as a description rather than a moral limit. The reading governs by extension rather than exclusion: it requires safeguarding frameworks to cover whatever persons exist, legitimates enhancement as continuous with flourishing, and leaves rival dignity readings legal, speakable, and publishable. This story is one member of a three-reading constraint family (with imago_dei and autonomy_rights siblings); its epsilon is authored for the standing arrangement under contest — the constitution-inclusive dignity regime this reading instantiates — assessed by the reading's own lights, per the kernel-reading epsilon referent rule. The claim/metric relationship is deliberately unreconciled: claimed_type is authored from the reading's structural position (a permissive coordination norm with no capturer and low coercion), while the metrics describe the arrangement's actual operation including its real costs to human-exceptionalist institutions; the engine computes per-seat classifications from the structural data and measures any divergence.
key_agents: synthetic_persons: primary protected claimant (powerless/trapped) — their moral status exists only if this reading's recognition holds
enhanced_persons: protected claimant (moderate/constrained) — living past the biological baseline rival readings treat as the boundary
unenhanced_biological_persons: covered claimant (moderate/constrained) — full dignity retained, diffuse opportunity cost borne
transhumanist_advocacy_communities: organized carrier (organized/mobile) — articulated the reading and presses its uptake
pluralist_governance_bodies: administrator (institutional/mobile) — adopt constitution-inclusive standards without enforcing orthodoxy
bioconservative_institutions: primary cost-bearer (institutional/identity_locked) — lose boundary-maintaining authority as the reading spreads
bioethics_governance_analysts: analytical observer — sees the full structure including the dilution critique
commentary.logic_rationale: Extractiveness 0.16: by this reading's own lights the arrangement extends protection rather than taking — the costs it imposes (standing and authority lost by human-exceptionalist institutions, diffuse opportunity costs of broader safeguarding) are assessed as removal of unjustified exclusive claims, not extraction. Suppression 0.15: the reading is pluralist by design — sibling readings coexist as live positions, and the arrangement holds through uptake and problem-solving rather than coercion; suppression is authored as the raw structural property it is, unscaled. Theater 0.12: where adopted, the safeguarding function is live, though performative inclusion (dignity-of-AI pledges without material safeguarding) is a growing minority share, tracked in the measurement series. Accessibility_collapse 0.22: understanding the claim forecloses no alternative — rival readings remain workable, so alternatives persist rather than collapsing. Resistance 0.52: substantial organized resistance from bioconservative institutions and human-exceptionalist traditions, partially absorbed by the pluralist framing itself. Both measurement series run on one shared six-point grid, with end-state values matching the base_properties scalars.
commentary.perspectival_gap: The seat divergence is the story's center of gravity. From the trapped, powerless synthetic-person seat, this arrangement is the only thing standing between them and moral-status exclusion — computed as near-pure protection. From the institutional, identity_locked bioconservative seat, the same arrangement operates as extraction: it strips the institution's boundary-maintaining authority, redirects standing to claimant classes it holds are not persons, and the identity lock makes the loss unbufferable — that seat should compute snare-or-tangled-rope-flavored effective extraction. The unenhanced-biological seat sits near-symmetric: dignity retained, opportunity costs diffuse. The engine computes this divergence from role, power, and exit data; the story-level claim does not adjudicate it.
commentary.directionality_logic: Beneficiary declarations map to low directionality for the claimant classes: synthetic and enhanced persons receive the arrangement's protection directly; unenhanced biological persons retain dignity and hold an unstigmatized enhancement option; advocates and governance bodies collect coordination and agenda benefits. Bioconservative institutions carry payer role with identity_locked exit, placing them near the full-target end — their effective extraction is amplified by the lock, though bounded by the arrangement's low base epsilon and low suppression. No directionality overrides were needed: the beneficiary/victim-plus-exit derivation captures the structure.
commentary.mandatrophy_analysis: The classification guards both failure modes. Reading the arrangement as pure coordination without the payer seat would miss the real standing transfer bioconservative institutions bear — their computed extraction records it. Reading it as pure extraction from the bioconservative seat alone would miss the genuine coordination function: the reading solves a live boundary problem that rival readings address only through coercion (imago Dei by exclusion, autonomy-rights by capacity tests). Mandatrophy risk is low while the founding problem is live. The dignity-dilution omega tracks the drift path by which the reading could slide toward extraction — if inclusive framing masked a zero-sum standing transfer, epsilon would re-measure higher and the rope claim would face reclassification pressure. The diffuse gain flow and prohibitive fixing cost here reflect live coordination value without a capturer, not atrophied inertia: theater is low and the founding problem live, distinguishing this composition from the piton signature.
commentary.kernel_context: This story instantiates the posthumanist reading of the kernel human_dignity_ai_safeguarding. Sibling readings — imago_dei_reading (dignity as the inviolable image of the Triune God, equal in all persons prior to any capability) and autonomy_rights_reading (dignity grounded in human autonomy, rationality, and rights) — are separate constraints authored as their own stories from the same kernel. This reading holds dignity constitution-independent and the human boundary non-moral-limit; the siblings would change the claimant class (the imago Dei reading subordinates claimant status to theological anthropology; the autonomy-rights reading conditions it on grounding capacities). The disagreement is located in the ground of dignity and the boundary of the claimant class (omega ground_and_boundary_disagreement_location). Foreclosure was assessed and rejected for both pairs: hybrid frameworks such as Christian transhumanism and pluralist-capacity views demonstrate a single party can hold layered versions, so the relations are coexistence, not foreclosure. The kernel has no single adjudicating authority — codification and authority grounding are both distributed, with no interpretation layer to declare.
